title: Composite latency-adjusted quality SLI and error-budgeting playbook for endpoints
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal:
Define a reproducible SLI and SLO framework that combines model output quality and latency into a single composite SLI for per-endpoint and per-model error-budget accounting. This ticket produces the playbook and enforcement rules for:
- SLI computation (latency-adjusted quality score),
- per-endpoint error budgets, banking/borrowing rules,
- automated escalation and circuit-breaker interactions, and
- rollout checklist and observability dashboards.

Why this is needed:
Current SLOs treat latency and model quality as separate signals which leads to conflicting operational actions during incidents (e.g., routing to a faster but lower-quality variant). A single composite SLI enables consistent decision-making for graceful degradation, automated fallbacks, and error-budget-based capacity borrowing across regions.

Scope and out-of-scope:
In scope:
- Define formula for composite SLI that penalizes quality by latency tail behavior
- Per-endpoint and per-model error budget allocation rules (including tenant-weighting for multi-tenant routes)
- Interaction rules with circuit breakers and regional failover (how composite SLI triggers load-shedding)
- Observable metrics, dashboards, and alerting thresholds
- Playbook for on-call escalation and rolling remediation actions
Out of scope:
- Implementing runtime kernel-level latency optimizations (separate infra tickets)
- Changes to billing or quotas system

Deliverables:
1) SLI definition doc with formulas and examples (chat/completion/embedding)
2) Error-budget allocation rules and simple simulator to validate policies
3) Dashboard panels and alert runbooks (Grafana + Console view)
4) Rollout checklist + canary experiment plan

Proposed composite SLI formula (first pass):
CompositeSLI = Q_weight * Q_score * f(L) + L_weight * g(L)
Where:
- Q_score: model quality metric normalized [0,1] (e.g., eval-set accuracy or prompt-based quality signal aggregated to percentile).
- f(L): latency penalty factor in [0,1] that decays quality when latency exceeds target. Example f(L) = max(0, 1 - alpha * max(0, P95_latency - target_ms)/target_ms).
- g(L): pure latency SLI normalized [0,1] (1 = meets latency target).
- Q_weight + L_weight = 1 (configurable per endpoint).

Notes on Q_score sources:
- For deterministic endpoints (embeddings): cosine-consistency and reference-pair tests.
- For generation/chat: combined automated evals (BLEU/ROUGE is insufficient) plus sampled human raters.
- Use continuous evaluation harness (see Confluence link below) to compute daily Q_score per model-version/route.

Error budget allocation rules (high level):
- Base allocation: each endpoint-model gets an error budget proportional to expected qps-weighted traffic and a risk factor (customer tier).
- Banking: unused error budget up to 2x base can be banked for 30 days. Banking only allowed for non-security incidents.
- Borrowing: Regions may borrow up to 20% of another region's error budget under capacity shortage; borrowing requires an automated rollback window (72h) and post-incident review.
- Emergency expunge: SRE lead can reset budgets in cross-region catastrophes (documented in runbook).

Circuit-breaker & load-shedding integration:
- Composite SLI falls below critical threshold -> trigger soft-circuit: preferentially route to variants with better composite SLI or drop low-priority requests (tenant-priority).
- If composite SLI degrades primarily due to latency (g(L) low) but Q_score still high, prioritize routing to low-latency hardware variants and increase batching tolerance where latency headroom exists.
- If Q_score drops (model quality regression) while latency is OK, trigger automated model-variant rollback and disable quantization-batched routes as pre-emptive remediation.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds map to error-budget burn rate: e.g., burn rate > 4x -> open CB for low-priority traffic.

Observability & alerts:
- New metrics to publish per route-model-version: composite_sli, q_score, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_budget_remaining_pct, error_budget_burn_rate.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO overview, regional borrow/supply map, and incident history.
- Alerts: fire at warning (error_budget_remaining_pct < 30%) and critical (< 5% OR burn_rate > 4x).

Rollout plan (canary):
1) Implement SLI computation in staging and validate with historical telemetry (2 weeks)
2) Deploy dashboards and retrospective simulator to SRE team (1 week)
3) Canary: enable composite SLI enforcement for 5% of traffic for internal customers only (2 weeks)
4) Expand to 20% with automated soft-circuit actions enabled (2 weeks)
5) Full rollout after 1 post-canary review and safety window (1 week)

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented SLI formula with examples for at least 3 endpoint types
- Prototype composite_sli metric emitted in staging for last 60 days
- Simulator demonstrating expected burn/bank/borrow behavior on historical incident traces
- Dashboard panels and at least two alert rules created in Console/Grafana
- Runbook and on-call playbook approved by SRE and Product leads

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Composite+SLI+Playbook
- GitHub (simulator prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/slo-simulator/pull/112
- Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/SL0/composite-sli-overview
- Incident learnings (Aug 2025): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=incident-2025-08-kvcache-latency

Open questions & trade-offs:
- Quality signal lag: Q_score may be noisy and lagging; how to weight real-time quality probes vs batched evaluation?
  Decision: start with Q_weight=0.7 for high-sensitivity endpoints and use smoothing (7-day EWMA).
- Banking caps: banking encourages risk accumulation. Trade-off: usefulness in absorbing transient spikes vs encouraging deferred fixes.
  Decision: conservative cap (2x) and strict audit for banking > base.
- Tenant fairness: high-traffic tenants could monopolize borrowed budgets. Trade-off: availability vs fairness.
  Decision: implement tenant-priority buckets and backpressure low-priority tenants first.

Next steps (owner: Ethan Li):

- Week 2: implement simulator and validate against 6 months of metrics (Eng reliability team)
